props.title: Fixing the Squash

B28.capture_spec: C15: Lab rect (ColorRect filling a 640x360 logical canvas, rendered at 3840x2160), lab-shaders/12-disc.gdshader. Keyframes (L about 10.2 s): radius = 0 until 0.56 L, then 0 to 0.8 over 0.56-0.80 L, hold. Render L + 1 s, 30 fps, Forward+. End state: teal bounding box 512 x 288 of 640 x 360 (measure.py bbox disc-640x360-oval; the same in Compatibility).
B28.visual_intent: Act title 'Fixing the Squash' (serif 40) top-left. Code card at left with the same disc shader as before; at right a real Godot window filling a 16:9 frame, empty at first, ringed as 'the wide shape' (readout '16 : 9'); then, as the voice reveals the result, a teal oval grows as the radius readout sweeps from 0 to 0.8. A terracotta ring settles around the oval.
B28.motion_claim: The oval grows from nothing on the wide shape, as wide-to-tall as the shape itself.

show.event: ring on the wide empty frame: 16 : 9
the radius grows; an oval grows

B28.runner_up: manim: an ellipse over a rectangle
B28.why: The oval appearing from the same code on a wide shape, after the viewer has predicted, is the problem; a real render proves it is not a drawing artifact.
B28.sparse_reason: The wide result window is deliberately empty and ringed until the oval grows (the viewer predicts first); the code card fills the other half.

B29.visual_intent: A 16:9 rectangle labelled 'the shape' with tick marks every tenth along its top and left edges. The first tenth by tenth cell at the top left is outlined in terracotta: a wide box. A bracket over the top edge reads '64 px', a bracket down the left edge reads '36 px'. Small grey credit: 'Godot 4.7.2 · Forward+ · 640 × 360 window'.
B29.motion_claim: The ticks draw in, the first cell lights up as a wide box and its two brackets measure it.

show.event: the rectangle and the tenth ticks
the cell hops to two more places: every cell is the same wide box

B29.why: Tick marks every tenth with pixel counts make the unequal steps countable.

B30.visual_intent: The same 16:9 rectangle with the teal oval drawn over it, centered. A terracotta arrow from the middle to the right end of the oval tagged '0.8 = 256 px' and one from the middle up tagged '0.8 = 144 px'; then outer brackets '512 px' across and '288 px' down. Small grey credit: 'Godot 4.7.2 · Forward+ and Compatibility · 640 × 360 window'.
B30.motion_claim: The oval grows, the two radius arrows reach out unequally, and the outer brackets read 512 and 288.

show.event: the oval grows from the middle

B30.why: A radius arrow in each direction with its pixel length, then the measured box, turns 'oval' into numbers.

B31.visual_intent: A grid of equal outline squares labelled 'square pixels' (each drawn square stands for four pixels, noted in a grey credit line). Two terracotta brackets cross the grid: a long one across, tagged '64 px', and a short one down, tagged '36 px', both for one tenth of the address.
B31.motion_claim: The squares settle; the long bracket and the short bracket then measure the same address step differently.

show.event: the short bracket down: fewer squares for the same step

B31.why: A grid of equal squares crossed by a long and a short bracket separates 'pixels are square' from 'address steps are not'.

B32.visual_intent: The wide address cell from the previous drawing (64 by 36 px) with a tag 'x aspect' and a definition line 'aspect ratio: width divided by height = 640 / 360'. The wide cell squeezes horizontally into a square cell labelled '36 × 36 px'.
B32.motion_claim: The wide cell squeezes into a square while the definition of aspect ratio lands.

show.event: the x aspect tag; the cell squeezes into a square (settled by 0.45)
definition: aspect ratio = width divided by height

B32.why: The wide address cell squeezing into a square is the fix as a transformation; the render follows in B33.

B33.capture_spec: C16: Lab rect (640x360 logical canvas, rendered at 3840x2160), lab-shaders/16-disc-aspect.gdshader, radius 0.8. Keyframes (L about 11.2 s): aspect = 1.0 until 0.50 L, then 1.0 to 1.7778 over 0.50-0.76 L, hold. Render L + 1 s, 30 fps, Forward+. End state: teal bounding box 288 x 288 (measure.py bbox disc-aspect-640x360-round; the same in Compatibility).
B33.visual_intent: Code card at left with the corrected disc shader; at right a real Godot window filling a 16:9 frame showing the oval from before, which turns into a circle as the aspect readout sweeps from 1 to 1.78. A terracotta ring settles on the circle with the readout '288 × 288'.
B33.motion_claim: The oval turns into a circle as aspect goes from one to one point seven eight.

show.event: aspect rises; the oval turns into a circle

B33.why: The oval becoming a circle as aspect rises, beside the one line that does it.

props.title: Tell the shader the shape's size
props.note: GDScript on the ColorRect · checked in Godot 4.7.2 (verify-aspect.gd, case A5)

B34.visual_intent: A cream code card with the real GDScript (the exact text verified in verify-aspect.gd): focus lands on the function that sets aspect from size, then on the lines that call it again whenever the node is resized.
B34.motion_claim: Line focus lands on the set line, then on the resize hook.

show.event: set aspect from width over height

B34.why: Real GDScript with paced line focus: set it, then set it again on resize; the cues follow the spoken order.

props.title: Where aspect comes from
props.note: Circle width over height, 1.00 is round · 2:1 shapes · Godot 4.7.2 · Forward+

B35.visual_intent: A four-row, three-column table of measured circle width over height, one row ringed as each source is named; 1.00 means round.
B35.motion_claim: The ring steps down the rows: the uniform row is the only one that reads 1.00 in both columns.
B35.why: A measured grid (four sources of aspect, two nodes) is exactly what the evidence table is for; the 1.00 cells are the answer.
